title: Loneliness, Friendship & Belonging
description: Explore being surrounded yet feeling alone through dialogue, evidence and psychological reasoning.

lessons.title: Company without feeling known
lessons.teach: Follow the conversation one message at a time. Notice what the behaviour might be achieving before you decide why it happened. About five minutes.
lessons.objective: Distinguish observable evidence from a tentative explanation of being surrounded yet feeling alone.

nodes.title: What might be happening?
nodes.body:
Loneliness concerns a perceived gap between the connection a person has and the connection they want. Avoiding small personal disclosures can reduce the immediate risk of rejection, but it also reduces opportunities to learn whether a friendship could offer deeper support.

Not every friendship needs emotional disclosure. Privacy and cultural expectations matter; the aim is not to demand intimacy from everyone.

nodes.title: One distinction to keep
nodes.prompt: Fill the missing word: An explanation of what a behaviour might achieve is a working ______, not a proven fact.
nodes.explanation: A hypothesis is an explanation that can be revised when observations fail to support it. This keeps psychological reasoning useful rather than turning it into confident mind-reading.
nodes.counterexample: Not every friendship needs emotional disclosure. Privacy and cultural expectations matter; the aim is not to demand intimacy from everyone.
